engine.meaning: Mostly the original verbatim, so nearly every fact survives, but two swaps change sense: "wash 60 heaps of dishes in your dishwasher" for 60 loads, and "Give a stuff about the width of the flapper" for "Pay attention to".
engine.sense: Several terms strain or take the wrong sense: "Give a stuff about the width" (the idiom is a negative, "couldn't give a stuff"), "60 heaps of dishes", "to ensure a beaut seal", "If any colour rocks up in the bowl".
engine.authenticity: Word swaps dropped into US agency prose: "Take a squiz at your water usage", "save water and the folding stuff", "Give a stuff about"; no Australian would phrase it this way.
engine.register: Far lighter than level 4: whole paragraphs left as written, e.g. "Leak detection and flow monitoring devices can help you identify leaks or alert you to irregular water use in a home".
engine.tone: Because it is mostly the original, the helpful advisory tone survives, though "Give a stuff about" lands as oddly flippant.
engine.flow: Readable since mostly original, with jarring inserts: "If any colour rocks up in the bowl after 10 minutes" and "to ensure a beaut seal and avoid leaks".
engine.variety: The little slang there is leans on "dunny" in every toilet line: "Dunny Leaks", "dunny flappers", "dunny model".
engine.essence: Recognisably the EPA guide, since it is mostly unchanged.

yarn-deadset.meaning: All points kept, plus metric conversions as colour on the given figures: "more than 9,300 gallons (about 35,000 litres)", "Make sure you flush straight after the test so it doesn't stain the cistern."
yarn-deadset.sense: "dunny flappers", "cistern", "Have a squiz", "the folding stuff", "get onto an experienced handyman" all fit.
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural Australian plain speech: "Fixing the easy household leaks can knock about 10 percent off your water bills", "to help people get their heads around the upside".
yarn-deadset.register: A plain, lightly Aussie rewrite; much of it is standard English ("Leak detection and flow monitoring gadgets can help you find leaks"), lighter than a level-4 brief asks.
yarn-deadset.tone: Stays helpful and practical: "Tip: Don't forget to turn the water off at the line before you start!"
yarn-deadset.flow: Smooth throughout: "Check your water meter before and after a two-hour stretch when no water's being used. If the meter moves at all, you've probably got a leak."
yarn-deadset.variety: Varied enough, though "gadgets" recurs in the device section: "Leak Detection and Flow Monitoring Gadgets", "tips for picking a gadget".
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the EPA guide: structure, headings, tips and figures intact.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point and figure kept with conversions as colour: "send more than 9,300 gallons (around 35,000 litres) of water down the gurgler every year", "replace it at least every five years so it seals properly".
yarn-dinkum.sense: "down the gurgler", "The usual suspects", "Have a squiz", "a once-over", "get onto an experienced handyman" all carry the right sense.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like a local explaining it: "No word of a lie", "Swapping one over is a quick, easy fix that saves you water and the folding stuff."
yarn-dinkum.register: A chatty Aussie retelling ("Good news is they're often easy to fix"), at about level 4, a touch restrained in the device section.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the friendly, practical advice: "Tip: While you're at it, it's a good idea to check the washer or \"o\" ring inside the showerhead too".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads naturally aloud, with one slightly topicalised line: "Pipe tape, also called teflon tape, you can get at most hardware shops".
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "No word of a lie", "The usual suspects", "Good news is", "Give the tap washers and pipe fittings a once-over", "While you're at it".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the EPA guide retold, headings and tips kept.

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every fact and figure kept; additions are reactions to the original: "Every year!", "One little drip!", "like it's haunted", "or you'll be wearing it!", "Not bad for an arvo's tinkering."
yarn-troppo.sense: "down the gurgler", "easy as", "a bit suss", "keeping it ticking over", "if it hasn't gone walkabout", "don't muck about" all fit their contexts.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Sounds like a real Aussie handyman: "the lot pays for itself in the water you stop chucking away", "then you go hunting for where the bugger's coming from".
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-4 voice ("Strewth, where do I start?") with swearing at dad level: "where the bugger's coming from".
yarn-troppo.tone: The helpful, practical advice comes through, though the frequent exclamations ("Every year!", "One little drip!") push it toward a jokey rant in places.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads like spoken advice: "Check your water meter, then leave it two hours with nobody using a drop, and check it again."
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied slang, but the exclamatory asides are a noticeable tic: "Every year!", "One little drip!", "or you'll be wearing it!"
yarn-troppo.essence: Still clearly the EPA leak guide, every section and tip kept.

unharnessed.meaning: All points kept: "more than 9,300 gallons of water a year", "replace it at least every five years", though the last tip drops "at the line": "Don't forget to turn the water off before you get stuck in!"
unharnessed.sense: Most fit ("a doddle to fix", "clapped-out", "get stuck in"), but "save you water and a bit of coin" uses a US money term and "Suss out toilet leaks by dropping a few drops" strains.
unharnessed.authenticity: Mixes Aussie with US and British forms: "first you've gotta work out", "to help folks get their heads around", "a bit of coin", "a doddle", and keeps "Toilet Leaks" beside "dunny".
unharnessed.register: A chatty level-4 retelling ("track down where the bugger's coming from", "strewth!"), with vulgarity within dad level.
unharnessed.tone: Practical advisory tone kept: "Tip: While you're at it, it's a good idea to check and, if need be, replace the washer".
unharnessed.flow: Mostly smooth, with a repeat in "Suss out toilet leaks by dropping a few drops" and a tacked-on "That's enough water for more than 180 showers, strewth!"
unharnessed.variety: Reasonably varied ("chew through", "chucking away", "a doddle", "clapped-out", "get on the blower"), though toilet/dunny switches without pattern.

summaries.engine: Mostly the untouched original with a few word swaps, several of them in the wrong sense.
summaries.yarn-deadset: Clean, faithful and natural, with helpful metric conversions, but closer to level 3 than 4.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: A natural, faithful level-4 retelling that keeps the guide's practical tone.
summaries.yarn-troppo: The liveliest and most authentic level-4 voice, keeping every fact; the exclamatory asides are slightly overused.
summaries.unharnessed: A decent level-4 retelling, faithful, but with a scatter of American and British forms.
